nodes.summary: Given a list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers and natural numbers $u$ and $v$, the boolean adjacency of $u$ and $v$ in $E$ is true exactly when $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ occurs in $E$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in an edge coloring edge list

nodes.summary: The EDGE COLORING decision problem accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of edge coloring instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.
nodes.title: EDGE COLORING as a decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $(n, E, K)$ be an edge coloring instance with edge list $E = (e_0, \dots, e_{m-1})$, where the endpoints of a pair $(x, y)$ are $x$ and $y$. The instance is feasible when there is a list $(c_0, \dots, c_{m-1})$ of natural numbers with $c_j < K$ for every $j$ such that $c_a \ne c_b$ for all distinct $a, b < m$ for which $e_a$ and $e_b$ share an endpoint.
nodes.title: Feasible edge coloring instances

nodes.summary: An instance of EDGE COLORING is a triple $(n, E, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$, the number of vertices, a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, the edges, and a natural number $K$, the bound on the number of colors.
nodes.title: Edge coloring instances

nodes.summary: The EDGE COLORING decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: EDGE COLORING is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An edge coloring instance $(n, E, K)$ is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(a, b)$ in $E$ satisfies $a < n$, $b < n$ and $a \ne b$, and $(b, a)$ does not occur in $E$.
nodes.title: Well-formed edge coloring instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
